title: Care Coordinator
company: First City Nursing and Care - Agency - Permanent
description:
Care Coordinator - Swindon

Salary: 26,790.40 (40 hours per week) + on-call payments (OTE 31,500 per annum)

Hours: 40 hours per week + shared on-call rota, additional hours may be required to meet business needs

At First City Care Group, we are passionate about delivering outstanding home care that enables people to live independently and with dignity in their own homes. Our reputation is built on compassion, professionalism, and continuity ensuring every customer receives high-quality support from familiar, trusted carers.

We are now looking for an organised and proactive Care Coordinator to join our friendly Swindon office team.

If you thrive on forward planning, problem-solving, and creating well-balanced rotas that keep services running smoothly, this could be the perfect role for you.

The Role

As Care Coordinator, you'll play a vital role in shaping the daily delivery of our care services. Your primary focus will be planning and maintaining rotas in advance, ensuring customers receive seamless, consistent care from carers who are well-matched to their needs.

You'll also be a key point of contact for care staff, customers, families, and healthcare professionals responding to queries, resolving issues, and supporting high standards of service delivery.

This role is based on a full-time 40-hour working week, with a structured on-call rota covering weekday evenings and alternate weekends. The on-call arrangement provides additional financial recognition and makes a meaningful contribution to overall earnings.

In addition, there are opportunities to increase earnings through optional extra shifts and ad-hoc cover, where available. As such, the total annual income may vary depending on participation in on-call duties and uptake of additional hours.

You'll provide out-of-hours on-call support on a shared rota basis, delivering 24/7 assistance to staff, families, and customers. Managing a range of calls including emergencies, general queries, and staff sickness.

Key Responsibilities:
- Develop and maintain rotas that promote continuity of care and efficient travel routes
- Match carers to customers based on skills, experience, and location
- Manage last-minute changes calmly and professionally
- Respond promptly to calls, emails, and messages
- Record and escalate concerns, complaints, and compliments appropriately
- Work closely with the care team and management to maintain service quality

About You
- Minimum 1 year of hands-on care experience (essential)
- Experience in rota planning or scheduling (desirable)
- Strong organisational and problem-solving skills
- Confident communicator with a calm, professional manner
- Comfortable using care management or rostering systems (training provided)
- Able to work independently and collaboratively within a team

What We Offer
- 26,790.40 per year + additional earnings for shared on-call rota
- 28 days annual leave (inclusive of public holidays)
- Workplace pension scheme with NEST
- Ongoing training and career progression opportunities
- Industry-recognised qualifications
- Blue Light Card discount scheme
- Employee Assistance Programme (Health Assured)
- Local motor maintenance discount
- Refer-a-friend bonus scheme

Additional hours may be required to meet business needs.

If you enjoy planning ahead, creating structure, and understand how vital continuity is in care we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now and become part of a team committed to delivering exceptional care across our community.

All roles are subject to satisfactory references, an Enhanced DBS check, and completion of mandatory training. This role does not offer sponsorship. If this position is not suitable, we may discuss alternative opportunities within our organisation.

title: Data Cleansing Administrator
company: Alexander Mann Solutions - Contingency - Agency - Contract
description:
We are AMS. We are a global total workforce solutions firm; we enable organisations to thrive in an age of constant change by building, re-shaping, and optimising workforces. Our Contingent Workforce Solutions (CWS) is one of our service offerings; we act as an extension of our clients' recruitment team and provide professional interim and temporary resources.

Our client is a well-known building society with headquarters in Swindon; As one of the largest savings and mortgage providers in the UK, 15 million members are at the heart of everything they do.

On behalf of this organisation, AMS are looking for a Data Cleansing Administrator for a 7 month contract based in Swindon. Hybrid with 2 days per week on-site.

Purpose of the role

We are looking for a detail-oriented Data Cleansing Administrator to join our client's People Chief Operating Office team, supporting an important data archiving and decommissioning project.

In this role, you will be responsible for reviewing, organising and cleansing large volumes of data, ensuring information is accurately classified, securely handled and prepared for migration into a new archive solution.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong administrative and Microsoft Office skills who enjoys working with data, maintaining accuracy and contributing to a fast-paced, project-focused environment.

What You'll Do
- Review and cleanse large volumes of structured and unstructured data across Microsoft Office applications and electronic repositories.
- Identify duplicate, outdated, incomplete or unnecessary information and apply agreed data cleansing procedures.
- Categorise information for retention, migration, deletion or further review in accordance with established guidelines.
- Support the secure and accurate migration of cleansed information into a new archive solution.
- Review automated data cleansing reports, investigate discrepancies and escalate any issues or exceptions.
- Maintain accurate records of data reviewed, decisions made and actions completed to support audit requirements.
- Ensure sensitive and confidential information is handled securely and in line with data privacy requirements.
- Carry out quality checks to ensure data accuracy, completeness and compliance with agreed procedures.
- Work collaboratively with project colleagues and escalate any risks, data inconsistencies or technical issues.

The Skills you'll need
- Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Outlook, Word and PowerPoint.
- Previous experience working with large volumes of data, electronic documents or administrative records.
- Excellent attention to detail, with the ability to identify inconsistencies and maintain high levels of accuracy.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage repetitive, high-volume tasks efficiently.
- Confidence following established processes, written guidance and data handling procedures.
- Ability to maintain accurate records, document decisions and support audit requirements.
- Good written and verbal communication skills, with confidence escalating issues when necessary.
- Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
- Willingness to learn new systems, tools and processes quickly.
- Previous experience in data cleansing, data migration, records management or information governance would be advantageous.
- An understanding of data protection, confidentiality and records retention requirements would be beneficial.
- Experience supporting project delivery, data reconciliation, testing or UAT would be desirable.

Next steps

This client will only accept workers operating via an Umbrella or PAYE engagement model.

title: Train Planner
description:
Train Planner Swindon £25,500 £34,328 Permanent The Opportunity

If you're looking for an opportunity to play a key role in a growing rail operation while helping shape a newly established planning function, this is the kind of position that offers genuine influence from day one.

As part of a new regional Service Delivery Centre, you'll join a team responsible for planning and coordinating freight operations across the South region. Bringing together planning, control, and rostering activities under one roof, the new operation is designed to deliver faster decision-making, greater operational oversight, and improved service performance.

This is more than a traditional planning role. You'll help build the foundation that supports safe, efficient, and reliable freight services while contributing to the development of new processes and ways of working as the function evolves.

You'll be part of a newly created operation where planning processes, standards, and best practice are still being established, giving you the opportunity to influence how the function develops from the outset. At the same time, you'll gain specialist rail planning expertise within a business investing in growth, operational excellence, and long-term capability.

Whether you have existing rail planning experience or a transferable background in aviation, logistics, manufacturing, transport, or another scheduling-intensive environment, this role offers an excellent opportunity to build a rewarding career within freight operations.

Train Planner Responsibilities

Train Planning: Developing safe, compliant, and efficient operational plans that support the successful delivery of freight services across the South region.

Timetabling & Pathing: Constructing workable train paths and schedules that balance customer requirements, network capacity, operational resources, and service commitments.

Engineering Integration: Accounting for possessions, engineering works, access restrictions, and network constraints to ensure plans remain achievable and compliant.

Operational Coordination: Working closely with Control, Rostering, depots, and operational teams to ensure services are planned realistically and can be delivered reliably on the day.

Plan Validation & Compliance: Reviewing and validating plans to ensure accuracy, operational robustness, and adherence to industry and business requirements.

Ideal Train Planner

Scheduling & Planning Experience: Experience producing structured schedules, timetables, route plans, or operational programmes within a complex environment.

Constraint-Based Planning: Exposure to planning within resource limitations, engineering restrictions, access windows, or other operational constraints.

Sequencing & Problem Solving: Ability to resolve timing conflicts, prioritise competing demands, and develop practical, deliverable plans.

Stakeholder Collaboration: Experience working with operational, depot, resource, or delivery teams to coordinate planning activities effectively.

Compliance Awareness: Understanding of structured, regulated, or safety-critical environments where accuracy and adherence to procedures are essential.

Transferable Industry Experience: Relevant backgrounds may include rail, aviation scheduling, logistics planning, bus or tram timetabling, manufacturing production planning, or port and terminal operations.

Location & Working Arrangements

Location: Swindon

Working Pattern: Monday-Friday office-based with flexible start and finish times.

Train Planner Salary

Training Salary: £25,500

Qualified Salary: £34,328
